summary: Active binding takes a zero-marked patient NP or object suffix, with b- for a tether, material or attachment support; ʕal marks surfaces/body parts, l- can mark a support or overt agent, and b-ḥḏoḏe / ʕam ḥḏoḏe relates multiple patients. Do not equate these prepositions with new meanings automatically.

Reflexive ruḥ- expressions remain active III; plural patients tied together do not by themselves establish Detransitive morphology. Detransitive Infectum describes agentless assembly or hitching; Part. Pass. describes a continuing bound configuration.

The new Preterit-wa and Infectum-wa boxes contrast anterior dressing with habitual binding; the source English/German tense does not determine the Turoyo box. Animal antecedents of the short MAC Infectum-wa examples are supplied in the surrounding verses.
Keep the inherited ʔṣr filing and disputed etymological note. maṣ-/moṣ-/muṣ-, plain s and -w- variants are not evidence for creating new roots; no root relabelling is proposed.

The Nomen actionis section already lists tuṣiro/tawṣiro/teṣiro/tawṣoro and two noun uses (bandaging; bandage). Reader claims that teṣoro and tuṣiro create an Infinitiv box are rejected. The PrS wolf scene suggests broader restraint/seizure, but the noun’s exact lexical scope remains unresolved.

Existing Detransitive Infectum example ʔṣr.III.d.infectum.1 has Turoyo in the translation field and further verse material in its note, an apparent parsing defect. The related supplied MAC Material culture/93 passage supports the binding construction but does not authorize silently reconstructing the historical source record.
The maṣər/maṣri/maṣro/maṣre forms remain under inherited ʔṣr III. Root-etymology questions and yṣr/yyṣr overlap do not authorize changing the heading.

New conceptual linking and social connections are particularly visible in authorial framing and political commentary. Round-1 work-commitment and constraint proposals are retained; new labels follow 1b/1c separately in active and Detransitive lists.
Habitual binding is already documented by three round-1 Infectum-wa examples. Repeated new-box claims are rejected; two independent contexts bring the literal cell to five.
maṣro with past copula and maṣre with a negative copula describe states. Reflexive ruḥayye remains active III; no reflexive object alone establishes a Detransitive form.
At Jan 2341 the muzzles are bound to horns; at 5446 binding plus a turned rope describes traction. Neither licenses a separate muzzle or bonesetting sense.
Check the historical ʔṣr / ṣyr / yṣr division; retain the current heading until the editors resolve it.
Confirm JTM 4.3/11 maṣəllelan as figurative argumentative constraint and the segmentation of l ano.
Resolve maṣəṇṇo at MAC Ishaq Material culture/7: contracted Detransitive Preterit or predicative form?

Check maṣri (+det) at 59/79 against the paradigm. The existing thread-binding example ʔṣr.III.d.preterit.1 cites 59/79, but the supplied verse there is magical binding; its correct reference could not be determined.
Repair the field split of ʔṣr.III.d.infectum.1 from its original source; the present translation field is Turoyo.
Confirm the shortened Imperativ forms aṣiru/Asiru/Asirulle/Aṣər in PrS and the unexpected Mašəlla spelling at PrS 78/23 before adding separate paradigm evidence.
Check JTM 1.1/16 kmaṣiri and 75/64 komaṣəlle against ko-Preterit; both have been withheld from publication.
Check the argument suffixes in JTM 1.1/12 kmaṣrənne femayye, MAC NE məṣrówaynanne, 59/95 maṣrola and 116/46 maṣrinanne; do not resolve person/gender from translation alone.
At Lahdo The snake/8 Turoyo samo is rendered “blood” in the selected edition translation. Preserve it and verify the alignment of that prevention clause.
Compare source 75/132 maṣərle with inherited maṣəlle, 77/156 ṭeiro with the reported teṣiro, and PrS 44/9 ḥa1se with the edition before emendation.
Does riding/ploughing preparation independently lexicalize “saddle/bridle/yoke”, or is it contextual fastening? The current patch merges those proposals into binden.
Jan 99: is maṣrene a plural state plus copula, or an active form with object suffix? Excluded from examples until checked.
Jan 417: does binding oneself at an inn mean securing oneself, encamping, or something more literal? Only Jan 5604 securely supports rooting at a place.
Jan 12: confirm first-person singular plus plural theme in maṣərnən; the English inclusive us is not morphological evidence.
Jan 74: is the servant comparison physically tethered or dependent? Retain the wider obligation connection provisionally.
Jan 2558: are bandat restraints or dressings? The verse does not justify narrowing binding to medical treatment.
Correct das to the conjunction dass
rationale: The clause introduced after “nicht,” requires the conjunction “dass”; “das” is a spelling error here.

summary: Fastening mounts and draught animals, strapping weapons, dressing wounds, and tying a human into a draught team are applications of binding; no separate senses for each patient or task.
Detransitive physical binding includes assembled implements and masonry held together with lime; inanimate patient type alone does not create another sense.
A stance constraining the church supports round-1 active figurative constraint, extending the causer and patient types.
Servant/master dependence is compatible with round-1 Detransitive ongoing commitment; literal tether in the comparison remains possible.
Physical binding includes restraint, rope attachments, ritual rags and treatment of broken limbs. These are applications of binding already retained in round 1.
